subtopic: PROVISION FOR MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL BY TRUSTEES
speechtext: Order. May I suggest to the hon. member that he address the Chair.

subtopic: PROVISION FOR MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL BY TRUSTEES
speechtext:
I am sorry, Mr. Chairman, I was trying to refer this whole situation to the members who made the allegations. From then on, Mr. Chairman, the situation built up until it was possible to launch an investigation. As I pointed out yesterday, any initiative on the part of the government to launch an inquiry into the affairs of a union which was affiliated with the Canadian Labour Congress would have aroused the most terrible attack upon the government by all members of the Canadian Labour Congress. From then on the situation built up to the point where an investigation was made. That step was taken with the full co-operation, knowledge, and at the request of the Canadian Labour Congress, and 1 felt that that was the proper way to proceed.
The hon. member for St. Lawrence-St. George and the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre made references to statements which have been issued in Washington by Mr. Wirtz and Mr. Meany. I think it is important in this situation that we keep a cool head, as suggested by the hon. member for Winnipeg North Centre. However, I also think it is important that we put on record the tremendous interference by United States citizens and the United States government in Canadian affairs. When we were the government we were charged with bad relationships with the United States time and again, simply because we stood up for the sovereignty and the right of Canadians. The situation as it now presents itself today shows that the interference from the other side of the border is far greater than ever it was during the five and a half years we were in government. If you want to compare the present relationship of Canada and the United States with the relationship the United States had with the former government, we would be termed bosom pals during the time we were in office.

In Washington the United States labour secretary Willard Wirtz said according to a press report:
Canada-United States negotiations to establish a private trusteeship over Canadian maritime unions collapsed because the Canadian Labour Congress insisted that the proposed three-man trusteeship be composed of two Canadians and one U.S. citizen.
That, Mr. Chairman, is the reason they collapsed. Can you imagine the nerve of Mr. Jodoin of the Canadian Labour Congress asking for two Canadians on that board.
Wirtz told a press conference that the A.F.L.-C.I.O. had agreed that the proposed trusteeship be composed of one Canadian and one American with the third party to be named by a Canada-U.S. committee of four officials.
That is a matter that affects Canada and Canadian shipping, and the negotiations collapsed because they did not have their way. This press report continues:
"But the C.L.C. was insisting that the third party would have to be a Canadian", Wirtz said.
I said yesterday that Mr. Wirtz came here to plant the seed of disruption and not to clean up the situation in Canada. Now the cat is out of the bag. That is why he was here and that is why Reynolds, the under secretary of labour, was here following his visit. At the same time the A.F.L.-C.I.O. president, George Meany, issued a statement bitterly attacking the Norris royal commission which had condemned the leadership of the seafarers' international union in Canada. "The S.I.U. deserves the support of all A.F.L.-C.I.O. affiliates in its fight against the destruction of free trade unionism in the Canadian maritime industry", Meany said in opposing the Canadian government's proposal to establish a government trusteeship over the S.I.U. of Canada.
This was the finest hour, Mr. Chairman, of Mr. Jodoin and the Canadian Labour Congress. But I want to point out that this is the same Mr. Meany who in 1953 kicked Mr. Banks' friend, Thomas Gleason, out of the A.F.L.-C.I.O. and at a convention in Philadelphia called him the associate of hoodlums and gangsters. Now he is backing Banks and Gleason.
I want to submit to the house that the Wirtz and Meany statements bring Canada and Canadians to this realization. First, here is an undisguised challenge to Canadian sovereignty. Second, here are American attempts to discredit this parliament and an outright appeal for defiance of its laws. Third, here is a statement designed for outright warfare along the whole maritime front unless wiser and cooler heads prevail, as the member for Winnipeg North Centre pointed

out. Fourth, here is an indictment of this government's indecision and its subservience to Washington.

speechtext: Will the house leader inform us as to the business for tomorrow?

speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
subtopic: PROVISION FOR MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL BY TRUSTEES
speechtext: Tomorrow we will start with the second reading of the bill respecting the trusteeship which has just been given first reading. In the event it is completed during the day we will then take the two bills which the Minister of Northern Affairs and National Resources has been patiently waiting to bring forward since September 30. We will then go on with the resolution stage of the vocational training measure, and if there is any time left during the day we will make a beginning on the estimates of the Minister of Public Works.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
subtopic: PROVISION FOR MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL BY TRUSTEES
speechtext: If the trusteeship bill does not pass the house tomorrow, is it the intention of the government to ask for a sitting on Saturday to deal with it?

speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
subtopic: PROVISION FOR MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL BY TRUSTEES
speechtext: As hon. members will have noticed there is a notice in Votes and Proceedings which will come up tomorrow. I intend to confer with my colleagues and also with hon. gentlemen opposite and will endeavour as early as I can tomorrow morning to indicate what the government's intentions are. It might be that one can get an indication from hon. members opposite that the business suggested for tomorrow might be dealt with expeditiously. Certainly the government does not desire to ask hon. members to sit on a Saturday if that can be avoided and the public business done.
It being ten minutes after ten o'clock the house adjourned, without question put, pursuant to standing order.
